name: Probability from games of chance
summary: The problem of points and dice questions are solved by counting equally likely cases, then generalised into a calculus of chance and, with Laplace, an analytic one.

name: Pascal's arithmetical triangle
summary: The triangle and induction were used to compute fair divisions.

name: Wallis: interpolation and infinite products
summary: Interpolating integer-power integrals gave an infinite product for pi.

name: Elliptic integrals from lemniscate and elastica (Bernoulli)
summary: Arc length of ellipses and spirals and the equation of a compressed elastic rod led Jacob Bernoulli to the lemniscate integral, treated by analogy with the arcsine.

name: Huygens: evolutes and the isochronous pendulum
summary: The cycloid's tautochrone property and evolute theory tied curve geometry to pendulum clocks.

name: Graunt: life tables
summary: Bills of mortality were analysed to build the first life table; Halley refined it.

name: Newton: infinite series and binomial theorem
summary: Expansion of non-integer powers and functions as series supplied tools for quadrature.

name: Leibniz combinatorial logic
summary: Leibniz proposed a calculus of reasoning by symbolic manipulation, largely unpublished.

name: Leibniz: determinants
summary: Systems of linear equations were handled by an indexed notation for determinants, left unpublished.

name: Newton's Principia
summary: Central-force motion, universal gravitation and orbit theory were derived by geometric mathematics.
